fields.label: Legal Business Name
fields.helpText: The full legal name of the entity as registered with government authorities (matches your Articles of Incorporation or equivalent formation document). Do not abbreviate.

fields.label: ЕИК / UIC
fields.helpText: Issued by Registry Agency. 9-digit code for legal entities; also serves as tax/BULSTAT ID. VAT number = "BG" + UIC (9 digits for legal entities; 10 digits for non-residents/natural persons). Branches receive 13-digit derivative.

fields.label: ЕИК / UIC
fields.helpText: Issued by Registry Agency. 9-digit code for legal entities; also serves as tax/BULSTAT ID. VAT number = "BG" + UIC (9 digits for legal entities; 10 digits for non-residents/natural persons). Branches receive 13-digit derivative.

fields.label: Trade Name / DBA
fields.helpText: Any trading name, brand name, or 'doing business as' (DBA) the company uses publicly that differs from the legal name. Leave blank if you only trade under the legal name.

options.label: Дружество с ограничена отговорност
options.description: Multi-member limited liability company; minimum capital BGN 2 (~EUR 1); managed by one or more managers. Most common entity form in Bulgaria. Equivalent to a US LLC.

options.label: Еднолично дружество с ограничена отговорност
options.description: Single-member limited liability company; same capital and governance rules as OOD. Equivalent to a US single-member LLC.

options.label: Дружество с променлив капитал
options.description: Variable Capital Company; introduced August 2023, registrations open December 2024; capped at 50 employees and BGN 4M turnover/assets. Used for startup and VC-backed entities. Equivalent to a US LLC.

options.label: Акционерно дружество
options.description: Joint-stock company with freely transferable shares; minimum capital BGN 50,000 (~EUR 25,565); one-tier or two-tier governance. Can raise public equity. Closest US equivalent: C-Corp.

options.label: Еднолично акционерно дружество
options.description: Single-shareholder joint-stock company; same capital and governance rules as AD. Closest US equivalent: C-Corp.

options.label: Събирателно дружество
options.description: General partnership; two or more partners bearing unlimited joint and several liability for company obligations. Closest US equivalent: General Partnership.

options.label: Командитно дружество
options.description: Limited partnership; at least one general partner with unlimited liability and one limited partner whose liability is capped at contribution. Closest US equivalent: Limited Partnership.

options.label: Командитно дружество с акции
options.description: Partnership limited by shares; hybrid form combining features of limited partnership and joint-stock company — at least one unlimited-liability general partner and share-capital limited partners. Requires minimum four founders. Closest US equivalent: Limited Partnership.

options.label: Едноличен търговец
options.description: Sole trader registered in the Commercial Register; no separate legal personality from the owner; unlimited personal liability for business obligations. Closest US equivalent: Sole Proprietorship.

options.label: Кооперация
options.description: Cooperative society registered under the Cooperatives Act; open membership with variable capital; profits and governance distributed among members. Minimum seven members required. Closest US equivalent: Cooperative.

options.label: Клон на чуждестранен търговец
options.description: Branch of a foreign merchant registered in the Bulgarian Commercial Register; not a separate legal entity — foreign parent bears unlimited liability for branch obligations. Closest US equivalent: Branch/Representative Office.

fields.label: Business Activities Description
fields.helpText: Plain-language summary of what your business actually does day-to-day. A paragraph is enough — describe the core economic activity, not the legal form.

fields.label: Products / Services Offered
fields.helpText: What the business sells to its customers. Internal-use products (HR systems, IT tooling, etc.) are not the target here — focus on what generates revenue. Select all that apply.

fields.label: Countries of Activity
fields.helpText: Countries where your business has customers, counterparties, or operations. Include jurisdictions where you receive payments, send payments, or hold assets — not just the country of incorporation.

fields.label: Avg Monthly Transaction Volume
fields.helpText: Expected average USD value flowing through your Conduit virtual account each month, across all in- and out-bound transactions combined.

fields.label: Estimated Transactions per Month
fields.helpText: Expected average count of transactions per month through your Conduit virtual account, across all flows combined (deposits, withdrawals, conversions).

fields.label: Source of Funds
fields.helpText: Where the money the business expects to receive through Conduit originates. Select all that apply (e.g. customer revenue, investor capital, lending proceeds). Use the 'Other' follow-up for sources not on the list.

fields.label: Fund Flow Description
fields.helpText: Describe the typical end-to-end flow of funds through your business: who sends money in, what triggers the inbound flow, and where the money is ultimately paid out. One or two paragraphs.

fields.label: Operates on Behalf of Third Parties?
fields.helpText: Select Yes if your business processes payments, holds funds, or transacts on behalf of other parties (e.g. payment facilitators, marketplaces, escrow agents, fund administrators). Select No if all activity is for your company's own account.

fields.label: Revenue Coverage of Operating Expenses
fields.helpText: What share of your monthly operating expenses your revenue currently covers, on average over the trailing three months.

fields.label: Has Institutional Investors?
fields.helpText: Yes if your business has raised capital from venture capital, private equity, hedge funds, family offices, or strategic corporate investors. Friends-and-family or solo-angel equity does not count as institutional.

fields.label: Cash on Hand
fields.helpText: Total liquid funds the business currently holds across all business accounts (cash, money-market, short-dated treasuries). Excludes owners' personal accounts and illiquid or locked-up assets.

fields.label: How will you use your USD virtual account?
fields.helpText: Select every USD virtual-account use case that applies, even those that are infrequent. This drives risk-tier categorisation and monitoring thresholds, so being complete is better than picking only the dominant flow.

fields.label: Ever Denied a US Bank Account?
Subject to Adverse Actions?
fields.helpText: Yes if your business has ever been subject to regulatory enforcement, consent orders, fines, license revocations, criminal proceedings, or significant civil litigation — past or pending. Use the follow-up field to describe each instance.

fields.label: Politically Exposed Persons?
fields.helpText: Yes if any owner, director, or senior executive of your business is — or is a close family member or known associate of — a current or former senior government official, head of state, senior politician, judge, or military officer. This is the standard 'Politically Exposed Person' (PEP) definition. Disclose your own people, not your customers.

fields.label: Owners/Directors Adverse Actions
fields.helpText: Adverse-action categories that have affected any current owner, director, or senior executive personally — not the business entity itself. Includes past employer enforcement actions where the individual was named. Select 'None' if none apply.

fields.label: I, and the company for which I am submitting the information contained herein, acknowledge and agree that by checking this box and clicking Submit we are electronically signing and such electronic signature is legally binding and enforceable in the same manner as a handwritten signature.
Treasury-Only Certification
fields.helpText: Certify that this entity will use the Conduit account exclusively for its own treasury operations — not on behalf of clients, customers, or third parties. Required to enroll in the treasury-only product configuration.

fields.label: Primary Industry
fields.helpText: The single industry that best describes your primary revenue source, chosen from the current policy catalog. If the business spans multiple industries, pick the one generating the most revenue rather than the broadest category.

options.label: Accounting and Auditing
options.description: The business prepares accounts, files tax returns or audits financial statements for clients. This includes accountancy practices, bookkeepers, tax advisers and audit firms.

options.label: Agricultural Equipment and Supplies
options.description: The business sells or rents farm machinery, tools, seed, feed or fertilizer to growers. It supplies farms; it does not grow the produce.

options.label: Agricultural Products
options.description: The business grows, or buys and sells, crops, livestock or other raw farm produce. It handles the produce itself, not the equipment used to grow it.

options.label: Aircraft and Maritime Vessels
options.description: The business sells, charters or maintains aircraft, boats or ships. This includes aircraft dealers, yacht brokers and marine dealers.

options.label: Animal Shelters
options.description: The organization houses stray, rescued or unwanted animals and finds new homes for them.

options.label: Art and Antiquities
options.description: The business buys, sells or auctions art, antiques or collectable objects. This includes galleries, art dealers, auction houses and agents who arrange private sales.

options.label: Automobile Dealerships
options.description: The business sells new or used cars and light vehicles to the public. It may also take vehicles in trade-in and arrange finance.

options.label: Bakeries
options.description: The business bakes bread, cakes or pastries and sells them, usually from its own store.

options.label: Bookstores
options.description: The business sells books to the public, in a store or online. It does not produce the books.

options.label: Casinos and Gambling
options.description: The business takes bets or runs games of chance for money. This includes casinos, betting shops, lotteries, online gambling sites and sports betting.

options.label: Child Care Services
options.description: The business looks after young children during the day, at a nursery, a daycare center or a home daycare.

options.label: Construction and Development
options.description: The business builds, renovates or fits out buildings and other structures, or prepares land for building. It does the construction work itself.

options.label: Credit Card Companies (Issuers & Merchant Services)
options.description: The business issues payment cards to cardholders, or signs up merchants to accept card payments. This is card issuing and merchant acquiring, not the day-to-day processing of each payment.

options.label: Crowdfunding Platforms
options.description: The business operates a platform that collects money from many people to fund a project, a loan or a company, and it holds or moves that money. A business that only raises money for itself on someone else's platform is not this subject.

options.label: Dry Cleaning and Laundry
options.description: The business cleans, presses or launders clothes and fabrics for customers.

options.label: E-commerce (General)
options.description: The business sells its own everyday goods to customers online. It owns the goods it sells, unlike a marketplace that lists other people's goods.

options.label: Educational Institutions
options.description: The organization teaches students on a formal course of study and usually awards a qualification. This includes schools, colleges and universities.

options.label: Electronics Retail
options.description: The business sells consumer electronics to the public, such as phones, computers, televisions and audio equipment.

options.label: Entertainment Industry
options.description: The business produces or promotes live entertainment, film, music or performances, or manages the people who perform.

options.label: Fast Food Establishments
options.description: The business sells prepared food and drink over a counter, for customers to take away or to eat quickly on site.

options.label: Fintech Companies
options.description: The business supplies financial products through technology, such as a lending, budgeting, payments or banking app. Its core product is software or a technology platform.

options.label: Fitness and Gym Facilities
options.description: The business runs a gym, a fitness studio or a health club where members train or exercise.

options.label: Food and Beverage Industry
options.description: The business makes, processes or wholesales food and drink products. It supplies the trade rather than serving the public directly.

options.label: Freight Forwarding and Shipping
options.description: The business arranges the transport of goods for other companies, and handles the booking, the paperwork and the customs formalities.

options.label: Funeral Services
options.description: The business arranges funerals, burials or cremations, and cares for the deceased.

options.label: General Retail
options.description: The business sells a wide mix of everyday goods to the public, with no single specialist product line.

options.label: Government Contractors
options.description: The business supplies goods, services or facilities to government bodies under a public contract. It is a private supplier to the public sector, not part of it.

options.label: Health Care Providers
options.description: The business treats patients. This includes medical practices, clinics, hospitals, dentists and other qualified health professionals.

options.label: Home Goods Retail
options.description: The business sells furniture, homeware, soft furnishings and other goods for the home.

options.label: Hospitality and Hotels
options.description: The business gives paid short-stay accommodation to guests, such as a hotel, a hostel or a guest house. Many also serve food and drink.

options.label: Import/Export and Cross-border Trade
options.description: The business buys goods in one country and sells them in another. This includes trading houses, commodity traders and import or export agents.

options.label: Insurance Providers
options.description: The business sells or underwrites insurance cover, or acts as a broker or an agent between the insurer and the customer.

options.label: IT Services and Software Development
options.description: The business writes software, or designs, builds and supports computer systems for clients.

options.label: Janitorial Services
options.description: The business cleans buildings and premises for other organizations, usually under a regular contract.

options.label: Landscaping Services
options.description: The business designs, plants or maintains gardens, grounds and other outdoor spaces.

options.label: Legal Services
options.description: The business gives legal advice or represents clients in legal matters. This includes law firms, individual lawyers and notaries.

options.label: Libraries and Museums
options.description: The organization keeps a collection of books, records or objects and lets the public consult or view it. It preserves and exhibits the collection; it does not trade in it.

options.label: Local Transportation Providers
options.description: The business carries passengers on short journeys inside one town or city area. This includes taxis, private-hire cars, shuttle buses and local transit routes.

options.label: Luxury Vehicles
options.description: The business sells premium, exotic or collectable cars. It differs from an ordinary car dealership in the price and the rarity of each vehicle.

options.label: Manufacturing
options.description: The business makes finished goods in a factory or a workshop, from raw materials or parts.

options.label: Media and Publishing
options.description: The business produces news, articles or other content and publishes it in print, online or on air. This includes newspapers, magazines and broadcasters.

options.label: Mobile Network Operators
options.description: The business runs a mobile telephone network and sells airtime or data plans to subscribers. It owns or controls the radio network itself.

options.label: Non-luxury Clothing Retail
options.description: The business sells everyday clothing and accessories at ordinary mainstream prices.

options.label: Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs)
options.description: The organization works for a public or a member benefit and does not pay profits to owners. It is usually funded by donations, grants or membership fees.

options.label: Office Supply Stores
options.description: The business sells stationery, paper, printing supplies and other goods used in an office.

options.label: Offshore Financial Services
options.description: The business supplies banking, investment or corporate financial services to clients in other countries, from a jurisdiction chosen for its tax or privacy rules. A typical sign is that almost none of its clients are in the country where it is registered.

options.label: Online Marketplaces (High-value goods)
options.description: The business runs a website where other sellers list high-value goods, such as vehicles, jewelry, watches or art, and buyers purchase them. The platform hosts the sale; it does not own the goods.

options.label: Personal Care Services
options.description: The business gives personal grooming or beauty treatments, such as hairdressing, nail care, beauty therapy or massage.

options.label: Personal Electronics Repair
options.description: The business repairs phones, computers and other consumer electronic devices.

options.label: Pharmaceuticals
options.description: The business makes or wholesales medicines and drug products, and supplies them to pharmacies, hospitals or other trade buyers. It does not treat patients.

options.label: Precious Metals and Stones
options.description: The business trades in gold, silver, platinum, diamonds or other precious stones. This includes bullion dealers, metal refiners, gemstone traders and jewelry wholesalers.

options.label: Private Banking
options.description: The business supplies banking, credit and investment management to wealthy individuals and families, one client relationship at a time. It is not banking sold to the general public.

options.label: Private Investment Funds
options.description: The business pools money from investors into a fund that is not offered to the general public. This includes hedge funds, private equity funds and venture capital funds.

options.label: Professional Training Services
options.description: The business gives short work-related training or professional courses to adults and companies. It does not run a formal academic program.

options.label: Public Administration
options.description: The organization is a government body, an agency or a public authority that delivers public services or administers public functions.

options.label: Publishing Houses
options.description: The business selects, produces and sells books. It works with authors and brings the finished book to market.

options.label: Real Estate
options.description: The business buys, sells, rents or manages property, or acts as an agent in property deals. This includes real estate agencies, property developers, landlords and property managers.

options.label: Religious Organizations
options.description: The organization is a church, a mosque, a temple or another religious body that holds worship and serves its congregation.

options.label: Retail Banking
options.description: The business takes deposits from, and lends to, the general public and small businesses, through branches or an app. It serves ordinary customers, not only wealthy ones.

options.label: Securities Brokers and Dealers
options.description: The business buys and sells shares, bonds or other securities for clients, or trades them on its own account. This includes brokerages and dealing desks.

options.label: Social Assistance Services
options.description: The organization gives non-medical help to people in need, such as counselling, food aid, housing support or community services.

options.label: Sports and Recreation Facilities
options.description: The business runs a place where people play sport or take part in leisure activities, such as a sports center, a field, a court or a swimming pool.

options.label: Supermarkets and Grocery Stores
options.description: The business sells food and household goods to the public from a grocery store or a supermarket.

options.label: Telecommunications
options.description: The business supplies telephone, internet or data communication services, or the network that carries them. A business that runs its own mobile radio network is a mobile network operator instead.

options.label: Transportation Services
options.description: The business carries passengers or goods for hire, over local or longer distances. This includes car services, bus operators and general road transport.

options.label: Travel Agencies
options.description: The business books travel, accommodation and vacations for customers. Some also package and sell their own trips as a tour operator.

options.label: Trust and Company Service Providers (TCSPs)
options.description: The business forms or administers companies, trusts or foundations for clients. It also acts as a director, a trustee, a shareholder or a registered address on a client's behalf.

options.label: Utilities (Electricity, Gas, Water)
options.description: The business generates, distributes or supplies electricity, gas or water to customers.

options.label: Veterinary Services
options.description: The business treats animals. This includes veterinary practices and animal clinics.

options.label: Waste Management
options.description: The business collects, transports, treats or disposes of waste, or runs recycling operations.

options.label: Other
options.description: The main industry of the business is not in this list. Pick this only when no other industry fits, and then describe the real activity in the follow-up question.

fields.label: Operates in Regulated or Restricted Activities?
fields.helpText: Answer Yes if your business directly participates in or earns revenue from any activity on the current policy catalog. If your activity isn't listed but is regulated or restricted, answer Yes and select "Other" to describe it.

fields.label: Regulated or Restricted Activities
fields.helpText: Activities your business directly participates in or earns revenue from, chosen from the current policy catalog. This asks about direct participation, not incidental exposure. "Other" is composable with named activities — select it alongside any that apply, then describe it below.

options.label: Forex and Currency Exchange
options.description: The business exchanges one currency for another, or trades currency for clients. This includes currency exchange bureaus and foreign exchange brokers.

options.label: Informal Remittance Systems (Hawala)
options.description: The business moves money between countries through a network of trusted agents. A customer pays in one country, a partner pays out in another, and the agents settle the balance between themselves later.

options.label: Money Services Businesses (MSBs), Money Services Operators (MSOs)
options.description: The business transmits money for the public, cashes checks, or issues and sells money orders, prepaid cards or traveler's checks.

options.label: Payment Service Providers (PSPs), PSSPs, Electronic Funds Transfer Services
options.description: The business processes payments on behalf of other businesses and settles the money to them. Its customers are merchants, not the people who pay.

options.label: Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs)
options.description: The business exchanges, transfers or holds crypto-assets for other people. This includes crypto exchanges, custodial wallet providers and crypto brokers.

options.label: Other
options.description: The regulated or restricted activity of the business is not in this list. Pick this only when no other activity in the list fits.

fields.label: Ownership Percentage
fields.helpText: Direct or indirect ownership share in the business, including ownership held through intermediate entities. For tiered ownership structures, give the effective beneficial share at this entity — not the immediate-parent share.

fields.label: Nationality
fields.helpText: Country of citizenship. For dual nationals, use the citizenship matching the tax ID you'll provide; if asked about additional nationalities elsewhere, disclose them there.

fields.label: Tax ID Country
fields.helpText: The country whose tax authority issued the tax identification number (TIN). May differ from the person's nationality or country of residence.

fields.label: Person Roles
fields.helpText: Which capacity each person fills. Beneficial Owner: holds ≥25% ownership or otherwise exercises ultimate control. Controlling Person: a senior managing official (CEO / CFO / COO / General Counsel / President or equivalent), regardless of ownership. Legal Representative: authorized to sign on behalf of the entity. Select all that apply.

fields.label: Immigration Status
fields.helpText: US immigration status — only relevant for non-US citizens currently living in the United States. Skip if the person is a US citizen or does not live in the US.

fields.label: Tax Residency Country
fields.helpText: The country whose tax authority the person files personal income tax with. May differ from nationality (citizenship) or current residence. For multiple tax residencies, list the primary one.

fields.label: Ownership Percentage
fields.helpText: Direct or indirect ownership share in the business, including ownership held through intermediate entities. For tiered ownership structures, give the effective beneficial share at this entity — not the immediate-parent share.

fields.label: Nationality
fields.helpText: Country of citizenship. For dual nationals, use the citizenship matching the tax ID you'll provide; if asked about additional nationalities elsewhere, disclose them there.

fields.label: Tax ID Country
fields.helpText: The country whose tax authority issued the tax identification number (TIN). May differ from the person's nationality or country of residence.

fields.label: Person Roles
fields.helpText: Which capacity each person fills. Beneficial Owner: holds ≥25% ownership or otherwise exercises ultimate control. Controlling Person: a senior managing official (CEO / CFO / COO / General Counsel / President or equivalent), regardless of ownership. Legal Representative: authorized to sign on behalf of the entity. Select all that apply.

fields.label: Immigration Status
fields.helpText: US immigration status — only relevant for non-US citizens currently living in the United States. Skip if the person is a US citizen or does not live in the US.

fields.label: Tax Residency Country
fields.helpText: The country whose tax authority the person files personal income tax with. May differ from nationality (citizenship) or current residence. For multiple tax residencies, list the primary one.
